The World Bank warned that India could become one of the first places where wet-bulb temperatures routinely exceed 35°C.
Which of the following statements best reflect(s) the implication of the abovesaid report?
I. Peninsular India will most likely suffer from flooding, tropical cyclones and droughts.
II. The survival of animals including humans will be affected as shedding of their body heat through perspiration becomes difficult.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
x: Wet-bulb temperature is an index that combines both air temperature and humidity to indicate the actual heat stress on the human body. It assesses the effect on the body more accurately than air temperature alone. In global studies, a wetbulb temperature of 35°C is considered the upper tolerable limit for human life; at this level, sweat cannot evaporate to cool the body, so the body cannot dissipate its excess heat. A recent World Bank report (November, 2022) has estimated that India could be among the first places where, in the future, wet-bulb temperature may exceed the 35°C 'survivability threshold', and millions of people could face the risk of deadly heat waves. As per the report, India will witness rising temperatures and heat stress due to climate change and wet-bulb temperatures are projected to approach the 35°C threshold under IPCC's future climate scenario (RCP8.5) by the end of the 21st century over the Ganges River Valley, North-Eastern India, eastern coast of India, and Chota Nagpur Plateau. The World Bank report warning mentioned here mainly focuses on wet-bulb temperature rising above 35°C, which is directly related to the physical survival of humans and other organisms– not specifically to floods, cyclones, or droughts in peninsular India. Therefore, Statement I cannot be considered correct. Statement II directly reflects the survival-related impact on humans and other living beings due to wet-bulb temperature crossing 35°C. s: Which one of the following provides the cryogenic indicator of climate change?
x: An ice core is a core sample that is typically removed from an ice sheet, most commonly from the polar ice caps of Antarctica- Greenland or from high mountain glaciers elsewhere. As the ice forms the incremental building of annual layers of snow, lower layers are older than upper and an ice core contains ice formed over a range of years. The properties of the ice and the recrystallized clarification needed inclusions within the ice can then be used to reconstruct a climatic record over the age range of the core, normally through isotopic analysis. This enables the reconstruction of local temperature records and the history of atmospheric composition.

s: When did the IPCC Seventh Assessment Report (AR7) cycle begin?
x: AR7 began in July 2023; Working Group reports are expected from about mid-2028.

s: Which one of the following is an India-relevant finding of the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (AR6)?
o: India's warming is confined to its coastal regions
India has experienced no significant change in heatwave intensity
India is warming more slowly than the global average
India is warming faster than the global average

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the IPCC?
o: It conducts original research independently of published literature
Its reports are policy-relevant but not policy-prescriptive
It shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore
x: The IPCC does not conduct original research; it assesses published literature.

s: Which document accompanies each IPCC assessment report to present its findings for policymakers?
x: The Summary for Policymakers accompanies each assessment report; it is not a legally binding instrument.

s: Which one of the following correctly matches an IPCC Working Group with its subject?

s: The IPCC SR1.5 pathways require net CO2 emissions to fall about 45% by 2030 from the levels of which year?
x: The 45% cut by 2030 is measured from 2010 levels; SR1.5 was released in October 2018 and reaches net zero around 2050.

s: Which approach is inconsistent with the mitigation pathways described for limiting warming to 1.5°C?

s: Without immediate, deep emission cuts, when is the 1.5°C threshold likely to be crossed?
x: The AR6 assessment states that the 1.5°C threshold is likely to be crossed in the early 2030s without immediate, deep cuts.

s: In the AR6 mitigation pathway, renewables provide what share of global electricity by 2050?
x: The pathway needs emissions to peak before 2025, net zero by mid-century and 70–85% renewable electricity by 2050.

s: As cited in the IPCC AR6 India-relevant findings, by how much has the Gangotri Glacier retreated?
x: Gangotri has retreated about 1,700 m since 1935. 170 m since 1990, 17 km since 1850 and 700 m since 2000 misstate both the distance and the base year.

s: Shared Socioeconomic Pathways in AR6 replaced which set of scenarios used in AR5?
x: SSPs replaced the four Representative Concentration Pathways, or RCPs, used in AR5.

s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Ocean and Cryosphere — oceans absorbed more than 90% of excess heat
Climate Change and Land — food security
Climate Change and Land — desertification and land degradation
Ocean and Cryosphere — reduction in the frequency of marine heatwaves
x: The Ocean and Cryosphere report highlighted that marine heatwaves became more frequent, along with coral bleaching and fisheries impacts. The other pairs are correctly matched.

s: How does black carbon deposited on snow mainly accelerate glacier melting?
o: preventing solar radiation from reaching the snow
x: Black carbon lowers the albedo of snow, causing it to absorb more solar energy and thereby accelerating melting.

s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
x: SSP3 represents Regional Rivalry. SSP1 represents Sustainability, SSP2 the Middle of the Road, SSP4 Inequality and SSP5 Fossil-fuelled Development.

s: With whom did the IPCC share the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize?
x: The IPCC shared the 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore.

s: According to the IPCC SR1.5 (2018), between which years is warming likely to reach 1.5°C?
x: SR1.5 projected 1.5°C between 2030 and 2052, with net zero needed around 2050.

s: How much warming over 2011-2020 did the AR6 Synthesis Report record?
x: AR6 SYR (2023) assessed warming at 1.1°C over 2011-2020, with emissions at their highest ever.

x: SRCCL (Aug 2019) covers land use, desertification, degradation and food security; SROCC covers oceans and the cryosphere.

s: On which subject is the Special Report of the IPCC AR7 cycle, planned for 2027?
x: AR7, begun in July 2023, includes a Special Report on Climate Change and Cities planned for 2027.

s: What does IPCC Working Group II deal with?
x: WG II covers impacts, adaptation and vulnerability; WG I is physical science and WG III mitigation.

s: What did the IPCC SROCC (2019) find about marine heatwaves?
x: SROCC found marine heatwaves more frequent and oceans holding over 90% of excess heat.

s: In which year was the IPCC's Fifth Assessment Report (AR5) released?
x: IPCC reports: AR1 1990, AR2 1995, AR3 2001, AR4 2007, AR5 2014; the AR6 Synthesis came in 2023.

s: From which body, set up in 1873, did the World Meteorological Organization originate?
o: International Union for Conservation of Nature
x: The WMO grew out of the International Meteorological Organization (1873) and became a UN agency in 1951.

s: When was the Synthesis Report of the IPCC Sixth Assessment Report released?
x: The AR6 Synthesis Report came out on 20 March 2023, after the three Working Group reports of 2021-22.

s: According to the IPCC SR1.5 (2018), by about when must global net CO2 emissions reach net zero to limit warming to 1.5°C?
x: SR1.5 pathways cut net CO2 about 45% from 2010 by 2030 and reach net zero around 2050.

Investment of Rs. 100 crores as an initial corpus under

x: The Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) is defined in Article-12 of Kyoto Protocol of UNFCCC. Such projects earn saleable certified emission reduction (CER) credits, each equivalent to one tonne of CO2 which can be counted towards meeting Kyoto targets. AOSIS, LMDC and the Umbrella Group
G77 and China, AOSIS and the EU
BASIC and the Environmental Integrity Group only
x: India aligned with G77+China (largest developing-country group), the LMDC (of which India is a member, hard-line on equity and CBDR) and BASIC. s: Which of the following is NOT correct about climate equity?
o: India's per capita emissions are higher than those of industrialised nations
Developed countries emitted most of the historical stock of greenhouse gases
Developing countries argue that they need carbon space to grow

Inability to invest huge funds in research and development

Only military technology and concessional food aid
Clean and affordable technology and finance

s: Persons displaced by sea-level rise fall outside the scope of which of the following?

only crude oil and natural gas

o: Room for developing countries to grow
Forest area used as carbon sinks
Carbon budget left for developed countries
